snippet.title: How do snakes swallow animals so much bigger than they are? - Niko Zlotnik
snippet.description:
Explore how snakes evolved, and find out how their jaw-dropping anatomy allows them to take down prey several times their size.

--

Since slithering onto the scene some 150 million years ago, evolving length and limbless-ness out of their ancestral lizard forms, snakes have diversified rapidly. Their noodly bodies and flexible heads granted them access to novel places and prey. And today, there are nearly 4,000 snake species, spanning habitats high and low. Niko Zlotnik explores how snakes evolved into incredible predators.

Lesson by Niko Zlotnik, directed by Anna Benner.

Below the turf, experts have uncovered a massive, ultra-fortified stronghold featuring a unique double-portcullis gateway and an impenetrable 14th-century "panic room." Built at the height of the Middle Ages, this architectural marvel was redesigned out of sheer paranoia to survive the bloody Welsh revolt of Owen Glendower. "World War II with Tom Hanks" is a landmark documentary event that reexamines the war through the lens of a new century. Each episode uncovers new dimensions of the conflict: the decisions that shaped the battlefield, the unseen networks that sustained the war effort, and the aftershocks that still shape our world today.

snippet.description:

Residents worried that it posed a public health threat, and petitioned the government for a solution. But where could they move millions of remains? Stephanie H. snippet.description:
The Lost Colony of Roanoke remains one of America’s greatest unsolved mysteries. In 1587, more than 100 English settlers vanished without a trace from their colony on Roanoke Island, leaving behind only a single word carved into a tree: CROATOAN. What happened to them? Were they absorbed into local Native tribes, victims of starvation, or wiped out by conflict? Or does something even stranger explain their disappearance?

In this video, we explore the chilling history of the Roanoke Colony, the theories behind the settlers’ fate, and why this 400-year-old enigma still haunts historians today.

If you’re fascinated by unsolved mysteries, history, and eerie disappearances, this is a story you don’t want to miss.

snippet.title: The dark origins of Disney fairy tales - Claudia Schwabe
snippet.description:
Dig into the infamous tales of the Brothers Grimm, and explore how these gory stories evolved as they spread around the world.

--

An evil stepmother demands a maiden’s lungs and liver; a girl is ripped from a wolf’s stomach; and sisters mutilate their feet to squeeze into a gold slipper. During the early 1800s, brothers Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm gathered these unflinchingly gory details from stories circulating around what’s now Germany. Claudia Schwabe explores how these now-infamous tales evolved as they spread worldwide.

snippet.title: The fascinating reason you loved peek-a-boo
snippet.description:
Dig into how the simple game of peek-a-boo contributes to babies developing their cognitive, motor, and social skills.

--

In Italy, it’s called il gioco del cucù. Palestinians say ba' 'éno. And in Japan, it’s inaīnaibā! Peek-a-boo is a near universal source of laughter and connection for infants and adults— it’s the first game that almost everyone plays. So what is it about this goofy game that babies love so much? Dig into how this simple game promotes the development of our cognitive, motor, and social skills.

snippet.title: Kate Burton Reflects on Growing Up in a Legendary—and Complicated—Family | Finding Your Roots
snippet.description:
When I sat down with Kate Burton on Finding Your Roots, we explored not only her lineage, but the deeply personal story of growing up in the shadow of fame.

As the daughter of Richard Burton, whose romance with Elizabeth Taylor captivated the world, Kate witnessed her parents’ marriage unravel in the public eye. Yet what she carries forward is not spectacle, but understanding.

Kate speaks with clarity about her father’s brilliance and his struggles with alcoholism, as well as the broader challenges she encountered within her family. Through it all, she came to a profound realization at an early age: that even amid instability, love can endure, and children can emerge whole.

It is a testament to resilience, and to the ways in which we come to understand our parents not only as figures in our lives, but as fully human beings.

snippet.title: Alex Honnold Climbs a 4,000 Foot Sea Wall (Full Episode) | Arctic Ascent | National Geographic
snippet.description:
Alex Honnold, a rock climber famous for his free solo ascents, and a team of expert climbers and scientists reach the final phase of their epic expedition - A 4,000 foot sea wall called Ingmikortilaq, one of the biggest unclimbed rock faces on the planet, and one of the most important glaciers in Greenland. In this full episode of Arctic Ascent from National Geographic, Honnold not only attempts the impossible, but helps gather critical field data with glaciologist Heidi Sevestre to research the impacts of climate change on the region's glaciers and the Renland Ice Cap.
